label: copy phase: input s while outputting z (s->z bigram recall), recall_idx>=3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is s (96% of mass; z inputs make up the remaining 4%). The strongest activations come when the original sequence has the bigram s z, so the step inputs s and outputs z; out_tok=z holds 80% of mass. It is absent for recall_idx<=1, weak at 2, and peaks at recall_idx 3-5. Never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter. Top examples (up to 3.5) are s followed by z, often as s z z. Copy-phase s inputs followed by other tokens (another s, 1, letters) give weak activations, which account for most missed steps (about 25% of mass). The predicate is precise (0.87 on dev) but recall is about 0.56, so the feature looks like a broader copy-phase s-input detector whose magnitude grows mainly when the next output is z.
